title: RNA and the Genetic Code
scopeNote: Original condensed MCAT biochemistry lessons covering the declared outline sections. This release is implemented, not independently scientifically verified; it is not exhaustive textbook coverage.

steps.text: The genetic code maps mRNA triplets to amino acids or termination signals. Several codons can specify one amino acid, but a codon generally has one meaning within a code context.
The reading frame defines successive nonoverlapping triplets. An insertion of one base in a coding sequence can change downstream codons unless offset by another event.
AUG commonly serves as a start codon and codes for methionine. Stop codons are recognized by release factors rather than ordinary aminoacyl tRNAs.
The code is nearly universal with important exceptions. Degeneracy does not mean every substitution is silent or that every reading frame produces a functional protein.

lessons.title: Control of Gene expression in Prokaryotes

steps.text: A bacterial operon can place several genes under shared transcriptional control. Regulatory proteins interact with DNA sites to change transcription initiation.
In the lac system, an inducer reduces repressor binding to the operator. Strong expression also depends on glucose-related cAMP–CAP regulation.
Low glucose favors cAMP–CAP activation in the standard lac model. Lactose availability and glucose availability contribute separate regulatory inputs.
Coupled transcription and translation is possible in bacteria. Do not transfer every bacterial regulatory mechanism unchanged to a eukaryotic nucleus.

lessons.title: Control of Gene Expression in Eukaryotes

steps.text: Eukaryotic gene expression is regulated at chromatin, transcription, RNA processing, RNA stability, translation and protein-turnover steps.
Enhancers can influence promoters through DNA looping and interacting proteins. Their action depends on cell-specific factors rather than proximity alone.
Small regulatory RNAs can reduce translation or promote degradation of complementary transcripts. Reduced protein output does not prove reduced transcription.
Compare DNA, RNA and protein measurements to locate regulation. An unchanged mRNA level with decreased protein can reflect translation or protein-stability effects.
